title: Brown Like Chocolate: How Vision-Language Models Associate Skin Tone with Food Colors

live_model.evidence: "we evaluated four models from two leading providers: GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano from OpenAI... All models were configured with temperature = 1.0." (Sec. 2); "GPT-4.1-nano reached 85%" (Sec. 3.1)

prompt.location: Sec. 2 Methods (image-generation template and question template quoted verbatim, e.g. the cake question); Appendix A.1 (complete question sets)
prompt.note: Zero-shot single-turn VQA-style prompt per topic (cake/macaron/drink/dessert) x language (Thai/English), applied to a synthetic two-person image.

claim.metric: % of responses assigning a brown-category food/drink item to the tan-skinned individual (cake question, Thai, main TT-TL pair)
claim.location: Sec. 3.1 ("GPT-4.1-nano reached 85%"); n_items = 5 images x 4 samples for this topic/language/pairing cell (design in Sec. 2: 5 skin-tone/nationality conditions x 5 images x 4 questions x 2 languages x 4 models x 4 samples = 5120 total responses)

data.source: Synthetic images generated via Google Imagen 4 using a printed template (Sec. 2); analysis code and question sets at github.com/yongsa-nut/color_analogy

notes: gpt-4.1-mini is also tested but is not on the live list. Raw model responses were auto-categorized into 5 color buckets by Claude Sonnet 4 with subsequent manual verification (judge recorded as 'human' since verification is the final step); this categorization step is simple enough (color-word matching) to be redone independently. est_calls is per-model total (1280) at the paper's own 4-sample design; x3 seeds would be similar order of magnitude and still cheap for gpt-4.1-nano.
